header.running_head: Conviction in the Promises of Allaah

blocks.text: Conviction in the Promises of Allaah
The Conviction of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) in the Battle between the Romans and the Persians as Promised by Allaah
Hadhrat Nayyaar bin Mukram Aslami (RA) reports that the Persians were prevailing over the Romans at the time when Allaah revealed the verses:

blocks.arabic_text: الٓمّٓ ۚ غُلِبَتِ الرُّوْمُ ۙ فِيْٓ اَدْنَى الْاَرْضِ وَهُمْ مِّنْۢ بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُوْنَ ۙ فِيْ بِضْعِ سِنِيْنَ ؕ
blocks.text: Alif Laam Meem (The people of) Rome will be defeated (by the Persians) in the (land that is) nearer (to the Arabs than the) land (of the Persians) and, after their defeat, (the Romans) will again be victorious within a few years.
The Muslims liked the Romans to be victorious because they were people with a divine scripture just like the Muslims. It is for this reason that Allaah says:

blocks.arabic_text: وَيَوْمَئِذٍ يَّفْرَحُ الْمُؤْمِنُوْنَ ۙ بِنَصْرِ اللّٰهِ ؕ يَنْصُرُ مَنْ يَّشَآءُ ؕ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيْزُ الرَّحِيْمُ
blocks.text: And on that day (when Rome defeats Persia) the Mu'mineen will rejoice about Allaah's assistance. Allaah assists whoever He wills, and He is the Mighty (none can defeat Him), the Most Merciful.

On the other hand, the Quraysh liked the Persians to be victorious because neither of them had a divine scripture nor believed in resurrection. When Allaah revealed these verses, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) went out of his house shouting:

blocks.arabic_text: الٓمّٓ ۚ غُلِبَتِ الرُّوْمُ ۙ فِيْٓ اَدْنَى الْاَرْضِ وَهُمْ مِّنْۢ بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُوْنَ ۙ فِيْ بِضْعِ سِنِيْنَ ؕ
blocks.text: Alif Laam Meem (The people of) Rome will be defeated (by the Persians) in the (land that is) nearer (to the Arabs than the) land (of the Persians) and, after their defeat, (the Romans) will again be victorious within a few years.

Some members of the Quraysh then said to him, "This will decide the affair between us and you (it will prove whether your religion is true or not). Since your guide assumes that Rome will defeat Persia in a few years time, let us place a bet on it. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) agreed because betting had not yet been forbidden at the time. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and the Mushrikeen therefore took a bet and agreed on the sum. They then said to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), "How would you specify 'a few' which can be anything between three to nine years[^1]? Specify a time in between so that we may have a time frame between us
The Arabic word 'بضع' used in the verse denotes any number between 3 and 9.
